newsitem.title: USA: Cigna reports increased second-quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Cigna reports increased second-quarter earnings.

text.p: Cigna Corp. said Wednesday it earned $279 million in its second quarter, up from $231 million a year earlier, as strength in its employee retirement and savings benefits business boosted income despite flat revenue.
Cigna, which earlier this week agreed to sell its individual life insurance and annuity businesses for $1.4 billion, said sales were flat at $4.7 billion.
The company said it earned $3.73 a share, up from $3 a year earlier.

On an operating basis, Cigna said it earned $270 million, or $3.61 a share, up from $252 million, or $3.28 a share, in 1996. The company's results were better than the $3.44 a share projected by Wall Street analysts surveyed by First Call.
Cigna's stock fell $2.25, closing at $195.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Operating income in the employee retirement and savings benefits business rose to $53 million in the second quarter from $44 million a year ago.

The larger employee life and health benefits business, which incudes Cigna's health maintenance organisation (HMO) and indemnity operations, had second-quarter operating income of $126 million, compared with $121 million a year ago.
HMO medical membership grew by about 280,000 covered lives, or 7 percent, since June 30, 1996.
Cigna said Monday it agreed to sell its individual life insurance and annuity business for about $1.4 billion in cash to Lincoln National Corp. of Fort Wayne, Ind.
